newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa consumers pause after buying at lows.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa consumers pause after buying at lows.

text.p: German cocoa processors retreated from the market after taking advantage of price dips over the last fortnight, traders said on Wednesday.
"The industry still needs to take cover but the strong pound discourages business," one said.
Chocolate manufacturers bought some beans and butter for 1997 and 1998 but stopped short of large-scale buying as they saw further downside potential, he added.
The London March contract on Tuesday traded near eight-month lows at 903 stg but bounced since and last traded near a session high at 926 stg.
Traders were divided over the pace of cocoa arrivals in northern Europe and the possible impact of dry weather in the Ivory Coast on the 1996/97 main crop.
Some said cocoa supply was abundant and pegged the crop on the high side of the estimated 900,000-950,000 tonne range compared with 1.2 million in 95/96.
But others said freight disputes were delaying arrivals in northern Europe -- with major shipments not due before November 25 -- and put the anticipated crop below 900,000 tonnes.
Local bean prices were 2.20-2.24 marks/kg for 1996, having reached 2.12 during recent futures lows, and 2.26 marks for first quarter 1997.

The cocoa butter ratio was at 2.78-2.80 for 1996 dates, unchanged from a fortnight ago. Implied butter prices liquid ex-works were 6.22-6.25 marks/kg. The first quarter ratio was at 2.70, with mark prices at 6.25.
Sterling was fixed in Frankfurt on Wednesday at 2.5090 marks.
